newsitem.title: USA: Berkeley, Calif., plans Nigeria boycott.
newsitem.headline: Berkeley, Calif., plans Nigeria boycott.

text.p: Berkeley's city council has tentatively approved a measure barring the San Francisco Bay area city from doing business with companies that operate in Nigeria to protest its military regime, officials said on Thursday.
The resolution, still in draft form, calls for the city not to purchase any products or commodities from Nigeria and bars Berkeley from contracting with companies that do business in or with Nigeria.
The city council approved the resolution in concept on Tuesday. The council plans to take a final vote on the measure at its July 22 meeting.

Fran David, Berkeley's acting director of finance, said five large companies were specifically targeted in the resolution -- Chevron Corp., Mobil Corp., Royal Dutch/Shell Group, BankAmerica Corp. and Coca-Cola Co. Chevron and BankAmerica are both based in nearby San Francisco.
"We could put the bans on the five major companies fairly quickly," David said. "It (the resolution) would apply to all new contracts and new purchase orders immediately."
Similar resolutions already bar the city, which has a population of around 104,000, from doing business with companies that operate in Burma and Tibet.
Berkeley, a well-known university town, has a reputation for being liberal and for being involved in political causes.
"Our citizens take their peace and freedom issues very seriously," David said.
